Definition: toiling; concretely, a laborer; figuratively, sorrowful
BiblicalUsage: Toiling, a labourer, and the Preacher hates his own labour for it. Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun, because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me. And the man alone, with neither child nor brother, labours without end, and his eye is not satisfied with riches, and he never asks, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good?
TheologicalSignificance: A word for the toiling labourer carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the question the Preacher never answers, for whom do I labour, when the labour outlasts the man who does it.
